solution: An array offers constant-time indexed access, whereas a linked list requires traversal. An array reserves fixed capacity; a linked list can grow node by node but stores an extra next reference. Inserting after a known list node can relink references, whereas insertion within an array may require shifting later records.

marking_points.criterion: Array direct access versus linked traversal.
Fixed reserved capacity versus dynamic nodes.
Known-position insertion relinks list versus array shifts.
